value.rationale: The source explicitly isolates exceptional narrow intervals where its boundary-suppression theorem does not apply. Determining their natural shrinking scale is a motivated structural gap. The result shows a qualitative crossover: suppression survives for every phase offset larger than inverse momentum, while order-one transfer can persist at inverse-momentum distance, with a closed Bloch-phase profile and a distinguished singular curve. This is more than a routine coefficient refinement because it identifies the boundary layer controlling when the transport conclusion changes character.
